newsitem.title: USA: Shipping cartel to raise trans-Pacific rates - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Shipping cartel to raise trans-Pacific rates - WSJ.

text.p: A major shipping cartel plans to raise rates on Asian imports to the U.S., the Wall Street Journal said Friday.
The move by the 15-member Transpacific Stabilization Agreement comes after a price war that has caused freight rates to plunge more than 10 percent in a year on trade from Asia, the report said.
The report said an exact rate hike has not been determined, but analysts expect the shipping lines to seek increases of between five and 10 percent.
The cartel, which controls 85 percent of the $200 billion Asia-to-U.S. trade, plans to initiate the increase in May but could face a challenge from Congress, the paper said.
Members of the agreement include CSX Corp unit Sea-Land Service Inc, APL Ltd.
